summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for severe nausea and vomiting, consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She had elevated blood glucose levels and required IV fluids and medication adjustments. A chest X-ray revealed a small left lower lobe pneumonia, likely due to aspiration from vomiting, and she was treated with levofloxacin and metronidazole. An EGD with Botox injection was performed, after which her symptoms improved and she advanced to a soft diet. Her blood pressure, initially elevated, normalized with treatment. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course, continue adjusted insulin therapy, and follow up with gastroenterology and endocrinology. Iron deficiency anemia was noted and recommended for outpatient monitoring.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
